claims.quote: Five such coaches were filled as I watched, and were shot up the guides to be locked on to their waiting packets three hundred feet nearer the stars.
claims.description: Airmail by postal airships, with detachable cargo pods hoisted up launch towers and locked into the ship's hull.

claims.quote: On the notice-board in the Captains' Room, the pulsing arrows of some twenty indicators register, degree by geographical degree, the progress of as many homeward-bound packets.
claims.description: Live remote tracking display showing the positions of aircraft in flight.

claims.quote: You can see it in the pictures of our racing professionals, from L.V. Rautsch to little Ada Warrleigh—that fathomless abstraction of eyes habitually turned through naked space.
claims.description: Professional air racing as a popular sport, with women among the racers.

claims.quote: Contrast this with the nine hundred by ninety-five of any crack liner, and you will realize the power that must drive a hull through all weathers at more than the emergency speed of the Cyclonic!
claims.description: Large rigid passenger and mail airships flying through all weather, with liners up to 900 feet long.

claims.quote: The eye detects no joint in her skin plating save the sweeping hair-crack of the bow-rudder—Magniac's rudder that assured us the dominion of the unstable air and left its inventor penniless and half-blind.
claims.description: A seamless metal-skinned airship steered by a precise bow-rudder that gives full control in the air.

claims.quote: Open the complete circle and she presents to the air a mushroom-head that will bring her up all standing within a half mile.
claims.description: A bow control surface that can be opened fully as an air brake to stop the airship within half a mile.

claims.quote: Magniac invented his rudder to help war-boats ram each other; and war went out of fashion and Magniac he went out of his mind because he said he couldn't serve his country any more.
claims.description: War goes out of fashion and is abandoned among nations.

claims.quote: The jointed U-tubes of the vacuum-chamber are pressure-tempered colloid (no glass would endure the strain for an instant)
claims.description: A transparent pressure-tempered colloid material far stronger than glass, used for windows and engine tubes.

claims.quote: Blessed be Sargent, Ahrens, and the Dubois brothers, who invented the cloud-breakers of the world whereby we travel in security!
claims.description: A worldwide network of powerful vertical beacon lights that pierce cloud cover to guide aircraft navigation.

claims.quote: Coventry Central, the pivot of the English system, stabs upward once in ten seconds its spear of diamond light to the north; and a point or two off our starboard bow The Leek, the great cloud-breaker of Saint David's Head, swings its unmistakable green beam twenty-five degrees each way.
claims.description: Aviation light beacons with distinct colors and flash patterns that identify each location to pilots.

claims.quote: Mail-packets are supposed, under the Conference rules, to have the five-thousand-foot lanes to themselves, but the foreigner in a hurry is apt to take liberties with English air.
claims.description: International air traffic regulations assigning altitude lanes to classes of aircraft.

claims.quote: A big S.A.T.A. liner (Société Anonyme des Transports Aëriens) is diving and lifting half a mile below us in search of some break in the solid west wind.
claims.description: Commercial transatlantic passenger airlines operated by companies.

claims.quote: Lower still lies a disabled Dane she is telling the liner all about it in International.
claims.description: An international common language used for communication between aircraft.

claims.quote: Our General Communication dial has caught her talk and begins to eavesdrop.
claims.description: Ship-to-ship voice radio that lets aircraft overhear one another's conversations.

claims.quote: We know that Fleury's gas can lift anything, as the world-famous trials of '89 showed, but its almost indefinite powers of expansion necessitate vast tank room.
claims.description: A newly discovered lifting gas of almost unlimited expansion and lifting power.

claims.quote: Even in this thin air the lift-shunts are busy taking out one-third of its normal lift, and still “162” must be checked by an occasional downdraw of the rudder or our flight would become a climb to the stars.
claims.description: Lift-shunt devices that adjust the lifting power of the gas so the airship can control altitude without dropping ballast.

claims.quote: The three engines are H.T.&T. assisted-vacuo Fleury turbines running from 3000 to the Limit—that is to say, up to the point when the blades make the air “bell”—cut out a vacuum for themselves precisely as over-driven marine propellers used to do.
claims.description: Gas-driven turbine engines turning multiple propellers to power the airship.

claims.quote: Even Fleury who begat it and, unlike Magniac, died a multi-millionaire, could not explain how the restless little imp shuddering in the U-tube can, in the fractional fraction of a second, strike the furious blast of gas into a chill greyish-green liquid
claims.description: A mysterious ray in a vacuum tube that instantly liquefies the working gas, giving a closed gas-liquid power cycle.

claims.quote: Bilge-tank, upper tank, dorsal-tank, expansion-chamber, vacuum, main-return (as a liquid), and bilge-tank once more is the ordained cycle.
claims.description: A sealed recirculating engine cycle in which the gas is repeatedly liquefied and re-expanded.

claims.quote: This means half a day's work for all hands and an expense of, one hundred and seventy-odd pounds to the G.P.O. for radium-salts and such trifles.
claims.description: Radium salts used as a routine industrial material for powering engine rays.

claims.quote: Our shaft-bearings are C.M.C. (Commercial Minerals Company) stones, ground with as much care as the lens of a telescope.
claims.description: Jewel-stone bearings for heavy engine shafts, supplied commercially.

claims.quote: And we are running an eighteen-second mile.
claims.description: Airships cruising at about 200 miles per hour.

claims.quote: Captain Purnall presses a switch and our signal beam begins to swing through the night, twizzling spokes of light across infinity.
claims.description: Searchlight signal beams used by aircraft to signal distress and warn traffic.

claims.quote: He has called up the North Banks Mark Boat, a few hundred miles west, and is reporting the case.
claims.description: Stationary aerial control stations over the ocean that receive reports and direct air traffic.

claims.quote: I've turned in a General Call, so even if they don't see our beam some one's bound to help—or else we must.
claims.description: A general radio distress call broadcast to all aircraft in range.

claims.quote: Her underbody colloid is open land her transporter-slings hang down like tentacles.
claims.description: Midair rescue using slings lowered from one aircraft to lift people off a sinking one.

claims.quote: Captain Hodgson opens the underbody colloid, swings the heavy pithing-iron out of its rack which in liners is generally cased as a smoking-room settee, and at two hundred feet releases the catch.
claims.description: A dropped weight with opening blades used to destroy derelict aircraft so they do not endanger traffic.

claims.quote: What if that wavering carcass had been filled with the men of the old days, each one of them taught (that is the horror of it!) that, after death he would very possibly go for ever to unspeakable torment?
claims.description: Belief in eternal damnation has died out of society.

claims.quote: And scarcely a generation ago, we (one knows now that we are only our fathers re-enlarged upon the earth), we, I say, ripped and rammed and pithed to admiration.
claims.description: Air warfare with ramming took place a generation earlier and has since ended.

claims.quote: We hurry into the heavy rubber suits—the engineers are already dressed—and inflate at the air-pump taps.
claims.description: Inflatable rubber protective suits worn by aircrew in storms.

claims.quote: Now under Tim's left toe lies the port-engine Accelerator; under his left heel the Reverse, and so with the other foot.
claims.description: A harnessed pilot station with foot-pedal accelerators and finger controls for direct manual flight control.

claims.quote: The Banks Mark Boat is reeling out pages of A. B..C. Directions to the traffic at large.
claims.description: Broadcast weather warnings and standing instructions issued to all aircraft.

claims.quote: The whole upper vault is charged with pale krypton vapours, which our skin friction may excite to unholy manifestations.
claims.description: The upper atmosphere holds krypton vapors that glow when disturbed by fast aircraft.

claims.quote: That old shooting-star's skin-friction has discharged the different levels.
claims.description: A meteor passing through the atmosphere discharges electrical tensions and ends a storm.

claims.quote: Those droghers will go anywhere on a chance of salvage,” George explained.
claims.description: Small aerial salvage and towing craft that cruise storms looking for wrecks to recover.
